note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 under the {partial} scope 44d59c79d4 added (independent judge, clean clone of HEAD 44d59c79d4). Section 5.1: "Because SGW will now see two possible SAs that lead to 10.1.2.3, it can become confused about where to send packets coming from Suzy's server.  Implementors MUST devise ways of preventing this from occurring." Tested ("Implementors MUST devise ways of preventing this from occurring"): a responder peer bound to a virtual-IP pool. assignVirtualIP leases from the engine-wide eap.Registry keyed by configured peer (one IKE SA per configured peer at steady state: a parallel IKE_SA_INIT supersedes the old SA in finishResponderEstablish); substituteVirtualIP narrows every proposed TSi to the lease host and refuses a bound peer holding no lease; proposeChildTSPayloads/proposeLeasedChildTSPayloads and answerNamesOnlyLeases keep a ze-initiated Child SA request and rekey on the lease. TestTwoPeersSameRequestedAddressDistinctLeases asserts two peers asking 10.10.0.3 hold distinct leases and distinct NegotiatedTSi, the second equal to its lease (responder established asserted in cpAuth). TestNoChildSAWithoutLeaseOnBoundPeer asserts no SA/TS/CP payload, no lease and an unchanged held count for no-request, CFG_REPLY and exhausted-pool cases. TestRFC3948ZeInitiatedRekeyNamesOnlyTheLease asserts the recorded proposal is the lease host, installed outbound policies name it, and pool-prefix, configured-prefix, wildcard and IPv6-pool answers are refused with errTSWidened and no child, with and without a recorded proposal. All 17 (sub)tests PASS at HEAD (./le job run, scoped -run). ./le rfc discriminate id RFC3948-5.1-1: four verified mutant records (assignVirtualIP neg, substituteVirtualIP pos, proposeChildTSPayloads pos, answerNamesOnlyLeases neg), none stale, none unproven. The proof reaches proposeChildTSPayloads through the rekey path (initiateChildRekey -> buildChildSAPayloads); initiateChildCreate calls the same producer but is not driven by a tagged test. Gap ("SGW will now see two possible SAs that lead to 10.1.2.3") confirmed at the producers: policyPairs returns nil for a peer with no configured traffic selectors, acceptablePairs accepts the whole proposed combination under an empty policy, so Producer internal/component/ike/engine/ts_narrow.go::narrowSelectors answers any inner TSi an unbound peer proposes (substituteVirtualIP returns the proposal untouched when VirtualIPPoolName is empty); dataplane/policy_owner.go::claim refuses only an identical policySelectorKey across owners and runs selectorsOverlap for transport mode only, so two unbound tunnel peers both proposing 10.1.2.3/32 install overlapping outbound policies. Overlapping configured remote selectors are likewise not refused (ordered only by PolicyPriority). Support remaining matches the row: it names the pool-bound mechanism, the same three tests, the unbound-peer gap at narrowSelectors and claim, the overlapping-configured case, and the owning fix spec plan/release/fixes/spec-ike-unbound-peer-inner-address.md (present). Zero whole-requirement credit; the MUST stays unmet for unbound tunnel peers.
